hook_text: Why do minibus brake discs glow after a long hill? Because stopping is just making heat on purpose.
clip_script: Disc brake: a steel plate spins with the wheel. Press the pedal, you push fluid, the fluid pushes two pads onto the plate. Small piston at your foot, big pistons at the pads, so the force grows. Pascal again. Friction slows the wheel and the motion becomes heat, hundreds of degrees on a long descent. Bicycle brake: squeeze the lever, pull a cable, two rubber blocks pinch the rim. Levers multiply your squeeze. Wet rim, poor grip. Both are controls: they do not drive, they stop. Judge them on stopping every time, wet or dry, and never failing quietly.
visual_style: Whiteboard disc with pads closing and heat lines; a pedal-to-caliper fluid path with small and big pistons; a bicycle lever, cable and pinching blocks; rain drops on a rim with a slip mark.
mood: Direct and a little dramatic, like a safety demonstration.
pacing: Glowing disc, pedal to pads, Pascal, heat, bicycle lever, wet rim, judge it.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and look at the brake blocks on a bicycle to see if they sit square on the rim.
